question: Should OpenClaw publish official signed standalone Android APKs outside Google Play, and which release channel, signing custody, provenance, and support policy should own that distribution?
rationale: Current main can build a signed third-party APK locally and the user impact is real, but publishing sideloadable APKs changes release trust, key custody, malware-confusion risk, update expectations, and support scope.

options.title: Approve signed APK release channel
options.body: Publish a signed third-party APK through GitHub Releases or F-Droid using the existing Android release/archive lane, with checksums, provenance, docs, and explicit support limits.

options.title: Keep Google Play only
options.body: Leave official Android distribution on Google Play and source builds, then update docs/releases to explicitly say no standalone official APK is provided.

options.title: Defer for non-Play store plan
options.body: Pause GitHub APKs until maintainers choose a broader F-Droid, AppGallery, or GMS-free flavor strategy for non-Play users.

recommendation.title: Approve signed APK release channel
recommendation.body: Publish a signed third-party APK through GitHub Releases or F-Droid using the existing Android release/archive lane, with checksums, provenance, docs, and explicit support limits.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current assignee and a recent Android app/docs contributor, while the final choice is product and security policy rather than a narrow code repair.
